scope: Pure camera helpers and native client-coordinate mapping. Conservative Float32 arithmetic is simulated on the CPU; no WebGL or browser rendering assertions.

nearEyeFloat32.note: Conservative CPU emulation, not GPU measurements. World Float32 vertex positions still limit close-range accuracy.

results.name: Original engine hash stays pinned and camera exports are available
Camera basis is orthonormal at high pitch, vertical and coincident poses
Orbit and eye-level poses use the declared yaw, pitch and distance
Perspective shrinks equal world spans with distance
CPU projection and normalized rays agree across viewports and screen corners
Project to ray to physical floor returns the original point
Horizon, backward, too-near and beyond-far picks are rejected
World matrix matches CPU projection and WebGL near/far clip convention
Eye-relative matrix matches world projection without translation cancellation
Sampled Float32 agreement at 8 km stays below .2 px beyond 5 m
Movement keeps cardinal, diagonal and analog speed as pitch changes
Native client mapping preserves DPR, letterbox, upscale and fractional offsets
Slab intersections cover forward, reverse, parallel and contained segments
Camera obstruction shortens the boom, respects ignore IDs and handles target contact

detail.containedTargetPolicy: Collapse to target; caller must ignore active interior box or choose a valid fallback.

results.name: Close wall never gets crossed by a minimum boom fraction
Repeated camera changes do not mutate native views or retain camera history
